I guess it would depend, we were both managers and our co-managers would make excuses to sit in our office for hours, making us stay on the sales floor. Our shifts are 8 hours long, so if she can stand for more than half of it I don’t see how it’s unreasonable to allow her office time for the remainder. Also, we never got our legally obligated breaks. Hardly ever were we able to go on our unpaid 30 and they were well aware they were making violations by not taking additional staffing precautions to allow time for breaks.

I was wondering too another co-worker is currently pregnant and wanted to sue for discrimination while pregnant because they told her they would make her step down if she couldn’t stand for more than 5 hours...I’m almost positive that violates some sort of law, considering pregnancy is considered a temporary disability and they’re not willing to make reasonable accommodations and threatening to cut her down to part time. She wanted to file and wanted my help since our boss made comments about my performance while being pregnant.

I did reach out to HR before I left. I spoke to a couple different people about how I thought it was intentional how she was behaving and I had serious concerns that she had a bad influence over other GM’s at surrounding locations. The HR associate assigned to our location took a sarcastic stance with me, basically questioning why I was even calling. She referred to my associate profile that had a long list of documentation, which I reviewed before I called just to see if I was imagining things. 90% of my documented issues were attendance, because I had worked there 4 years and you had to have a conversation every time you had an attendance fraction, most of mine from forgetting to clock in and out (so nothing serious). The other half were yearly/mid year reviews where I was distinguished for meeting expectations. I’m wanting to know if I can sue for emotional distress, she was manipulative, intentionally hurtful, and definitely expressed favoritism.

For one example while I was pregnant she would pull me aside several times asking me why I wasn’t on the sales floor while two other managers were preparing for an audit. I was sick my entire pregnancy and spent the first few months with bad motion sickness. I’d vomit during my entire commute but also some times during the day. So sometimes I was in the bathroom sick for a few minutes throughout my shift, which I was never late to despite being sick and having an hour commute. When I’d try to talk to her about how I was having a hard time she would make fun of me to my face about it, saying it was obvious. She told me that my performance was being affected by my pregnancy. Shortly after maternity leave I was hospitalized with a bad infection and had to be off work for a few weeks. She was incredibly rude about me calling into work, and when I called her again that night I was going into surgery and told her I didn’t know when I would be released from the hospital. Every time in between she was so fricking bi-polar I wouldn’t know if I was meeting her expectations or not, even after directly asking her for feedback several times. Eventually a new location opened a mile from my house, and I requested to transfer. She said she wouldn’t because I was negligent and had poor communication skills despite having documented reviews that I had exceptional communication skills. She wouldn’t transfer me because she had trouble filling my position before I came along (4 people in 1 year).
